The function is \( f(x) = \log(x^2) \). The logarithm is defined only for positive arguments, so we require \( x^2 > 0 \). This inequality holds for all real numbers except \( x = 0 \). Therefore, the domain is \( x < 0 \) or \( x > 0 \). Comparing this with the given form \( x < a \) or \( x > b \), we identify \( a = 0 \) and \( b = 0 \). Hence, \( a + b = 0 \).
